subject: Re: Post-call quant profile + $/1M token target
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena@storica.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap: token mix + pricing targets

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can put together a clean pricing proposal for Storica: 

Summary of what I heard on the call:
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + contextual agent for customer support (mostly English).
- Expected user base: 12k monthly active users, roughly 1.2M prompts/day at peak (bursty).
- Prompt profile: average prompt ~160 tokens (range 40–1,200 depending on user query).
- Completion profile: two modes — short (average 60 tokens) for quick answers; long (average 1,600 tokens) for threaded summaries/exports.
- Context window needs: most sessions fit in 8k, but 10–15% require 32k; a small subset (1–2%) are archival exports that could need 128k.

As discussed, the two things we need from you to finalize the proposal: 
1) A realistic weekly/monthly breakdown of the volume mix (percentage of calls that are short vs long completions, and percent of traffic hitting 8k/32k/128k windows). A row like: short-complete % | long-complete % | 8k % | 32k % | 128k % is great.
2) Target cost envelope: you mentioned a guide of "$40–$80 / 1M tokens" as your procurement target — can you confirm a target number (single value or band) so we can optimize model+quantization choices to hit that?

Attachments: I attached a template spreadsheet (storica-usage-estimates.xlsx) with the fields we discussed — if you fill the monthly/weekly columns I’ll run three cost scenarios (hosted; dedicated with reserved capacity; dedicated + quantized) and send back a short comparison.

Proposed next steps:
- Elena: add rough monthly volumes to the spreadsheet by Tue 12/22.
- Karthik: I asked him to sketch initial throughput/latency constraints for the short vs long paths so we can size Dedicated if needed.
- Me: I’ll model three $/1M token scenarios and show expected monthly spend and latency tradeoffs.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Elena Vasquez <elena@storica.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@storica.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 16:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token mix + pricing targets

Hi Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications and preliminary answers below.

Volume mix (ballpark, per month):
- Total prompts: ~25M/month.
- Short completions (~60 tokens): 85% of prompts (mostly single-turn replies).
- Long completions (~1,600 tokens): 13% (summary exports, multi-turn threads).
- Archival exports needing >32k (our ETL/exports): 2% (these are scheduled jobs, not interactive).

Context window: most interactive cases are under 8k (about 83%). ~15% need 32k to retain multi-turn context, and the 2% archival we mentioned need 128k for full document exports.

Target $/1M tokens: we are looking to be below $50 / 1M tokens as a procurement target; if you can show options around $30–$50 with tradeoffs in latency and quality that would be ideal.

Notes on latency: interactive replies need p95 < 800ms for short paths; long summaries can tolerate p95 up to 2.5s.

I dropped preliminary numbers into your spreadsheet and attached a quick summary (storica-usage-estimates.xlsx). Let me know if you want the raw query logs (we can share an anonymized sample).

Thanks,
Elena
Customer Success Lead, Storica Inc.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Vasquez <elena@storica.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Dec 2026 08:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token mix + pricing targets

Elena — perfect, that’s exactly what we needed. I ran a quick sanity model with the numbers you dropped in and sketched three scenarios (attached as redwood-cost-scenarios.pdf):

Scenario A — Hosted (managed):
- Assumes mixed model routing: cheaper short model for short completions, high-capacity long model for summaries.
- Estimated blended cost: ~$48 / 1M tokens.
- Latency: meets p95 short path target; long path ~1.6–2.0s.
- Pros: zero infra ops; elastic handling of bursts.

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved capacity (non-quantized):
- Cluster sized to steady-state with burst nodes for peak.
- Estimated blended cost: ~$36 / 1M tokens but requires monthly commitment and network setup.
- Latency: consistent, p95 short path <500ms.

Scenario C — Dedicated + 4-bit quantized long-tail models for exports:
- Quantization applied to long/archival model variants; short path uses FP16 for quality.
- Estimated blended cost: ~$28 / 1M tokens (best-case).
- Tradeoffs: small degradation on very long-tail prompts; we recommend accuracy regression tests (we can run on your anonymized sample).

A couple of open items I flagged in the PDF:
- Confirm if the 2% archival exports can be scheduled to off-peak windows (this makes quantized batch processing much cheaper).
- For Dedicated sizing, Karthik needs your average concurrent sessions during peak 1-hour windows (he’ll use that to size GPU pool plus burst).

If the $30–$50 band is the procurement sweet spot, Scenario B (Dedicated non-quantized) and C (Dedicated + quant) bracket it. If you want a sales-friendly single-slide comparison I can prep a one-pager for your procurement team.

Next steps (proposed):
- Elena: confirm whether archival exports can be batched off-peak and share a 1-hour peak concurrent number by Mon 12/21.
- Marissa: I’m looping you for pricing approvals and contracting path (SaaS vs Reserved).
- Karthik: please size a starter Dedicated config for 12k MAU and the provided concurrency estimate.

Thanks — I attached the scenario PDF and included the updated spreadsheet.

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-cost-scenarios.pdf (3 pages)
